days.heading: Depart Pittsburgh after work

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: PIT -> gateway -> FNC on one protected ticket

days.note: Same trick as every version of this trip: leave after work, sleep badly once, start the vacation abroad. The whole PIT-to-Funchal chain must be ONE ticket - via Lisbon on TAP, or via Newark if United's seasonal EWR-FNC nonstop returns for 2027.

days.heading: Arrive Funchal, cable car, old town evening
days.daycost: Est. $180-$320 - car pickup, cable car, simple dinner
days.note: Keep arrival deliberately easy: pick up the car, check in, then the Monte cable car and toboggan as the jet-lag-proof kid hook (toboggans close Sundays - today is Wednesday, so it works). Early dinner in the Zona Velha, early bed - tomorrow starts at 5 am.

spots.cost: Cable car EUR 22 RT / EUR 16 one-way adult, ages 7-14 half price - one-way up for the family is ~EUR 48. Monte toboggan (2026 prices): EUR 40 per 2-person sled, cash only, closed Sundays - two sleds = EUR 80. Monte Palace garden EUR 18 adult, kids to 14 free.
spots.climate: June Funchal: 72-75 F days / 61-63 F nights, ~10 hours of sun and only ~5 rain days - one of the driest months on the island.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride the cable car one-way up (EUR 48, not EUR 76 RT), toboggan partway down, and finish by Bolt/taxi - the classic route that skips paying for the ride down twice.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The toboggan itself IS the splurge at EUR 80 for two wicker sleds - a 130-year-old tradition and the single most kid-memorable EUR 80 on the island.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzaria Xaramba — old-town pizzeria by the fort; plain margherita is the safe order
  • Hamburgueria do Mercado — burgers and fries by the market; a plain burger runs about EUR 10
  • Il Basilico — Lido promenade Italian; pizza, plain pasta, and highchairs
spots.altboxHtml:
• Mercado dos Lavradores + old-town painted doors ↩ — the free version of a Funchal afternoon: market fruit tasting upstairs, painted-door street art in the Zona Velha, gelato by the fort.
  • Jardim Botanico da Madeira ↗ — terraced gardens and city views; a good fog or heat substitute for higher viewpoints.
  • Lido pools ↗ — easy managed swim with showers and food if open-water conditions are not friendly.

days.heading: Arieiro sunrise: Stairway to Heaven - weather shot 1 of 2
days.daycost: Est. $80-$220 - permits, fuel or transfer, lunch

facts.label: Permit
facts.valueHtml: PR1 EUR 10.50 pp, kids 12 and under free

days.note: The family version is the out-and-back from the Arieiro summit to Ninho da Manta and the staircase viewpoints (this first section is two-way; the full one-way traverse to Pico Ruivo is too strenuous for the 8-year-old). If the summit is in cloud, bail early and swap this with Saturday - that retry is exactly what the 4-night stay buys.

spots.cost: PR1 permit EUR 10.50 pp booked on SIMplifica (EUR 7 with a licensed operator); kids 12 and under free, so the family pays ~EUR 31.50. Summit parking free but full before sunrise on clear days. Shared sunrise transfer alternative: EUR 30-40 pp.
spots.climate: Pre-dawn summit (1,818 m): 41-50 F even in June - real jackets and hats. The sea-of-clouds inversion is a morning phenomenon; clouds typically swallow the peaks by afternoon. June is one of Madeira's driest months.
spots.saveHtml: Save Self-drive at 5:15 am instead of booking transfer seats: the family saves roughly $120-$160 and keeps the schedule flexible for the cloud lottery.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book the guided sunrise transfer (EUR 30-40 pp) if nobody wants to drive mountain hairpins in the dark - pickup ~5:00-5:30 am for a ~6:50 sunrise.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzaria Xaramba — old-town pizzeria by the fort; plain margherita is the safe order
  • Hamburgueria do Mercado — burgers and fries by the market; a plain burger runs about EUR 10
  • Il Basilico — Lido promenade Italian; pizza, plain pasta, and highchairs
spots.altboxHtml:
• Pico Ruivo from Achada do Teixeira (PR1.2) ↩ — the gentler back route to Madeira's highest summit - a real substitute if the PR1 first section is closed or the exposure feels like too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Risco waterfall only ↗ — flatter Rabacal branch with a tall waterfall when 25 Fontes feels like too much walking.
  • Queimadas Forest Park ↗ — thatched houses, picnic lawns, and easy laurel-forest paths without a long levada commitment.

days.heading: 25 Fontes levada, then Camara de Lobos golden hour

facts.label: Late day
facts.valueHtml: Camara de Lobos + Cabo Girao skywalk

days.note: Levada walking is the flat, kid-friendly counterpoint to yesterday's ridge: water channels, tunnels of green, and a waterfall pool payoff. Bail to the short Risco branch if the 8-year-old is done. End with fishing boats and the 580 m skywalk on the way home.

spots.name: 25 Fontes + Risco levada (PR6, Rabacal)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · 25 FontesIG · RiscoFlickr
spots.cost: Permit EUR 4.50 pp (kids 12 and under free) = ~EUR 13.50 family, booked on SIMplifica. Rabacal parking free; the access-road shuttle is EUR 5 one-way / EUR 8 return, cash only.
spots.climate: June: the Rabacal plateau sits in the cloud belt - expect cooler, mistier air than Funchal and pack a layer. Trails are mostly flat levada walking with ~300 m of stairs near the falls.
spots.saveHtml: Save Start before the ~10-11 am shuttle and walk the 2 km access road down (~40 min) - saves EUR 32 family and beats the crowds to the falls.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge None needed - this day is nearly free. If energy is high, add the 30-minute Risco waterfall branch (PR6.1) at no extra cost.
spots.restoHtml:
• Anonimo — some of the island's best Neapolitan pizza; margherita for the kids
  • Pizza Cafe (Camara de Lobos) — generous pizza and pasta portions steps from the harbor
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada house since 1966; grilled beef/chicken skewers, fries, and bolo do caco bread
spots.altboxHtml:
• Risco waterfall only (PR6.1) ↩ — the built-in bail-out: the Risco branch is a short, flat walk to a 100 m waterfall if the full 9-11 km round trip looks like too much for the 8-year-old.
  • Queimadas Forest Park ↗ — thatched houses, picnic lawns, and easy laurel-forest paths without a long levada commitment.
  • Ribeiro Frio and Balcoes ↗ — short, family-friendly forest walk with a big-view payoff if clouds cooperate.

spots.climate: June: the sunny south coast - 72-75 F afternoons. Golden hour is the move: fishing boats glow and the 580 m cliff view softens after the tour buses leave.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do this as the late-afternoon tail of the 25 Fontes day rather than a separate outing - it is 15 minutes from Funchal and needs no tickets beyond the skywalk.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge An espetada dinner at Santo Antonio in Estreito - the skewers-and-fries house the locals drive to, and a legitimately picky-kid-safe splurge.
spots.restoHtml:

  • Mercado dos Lavradores ↗ — colorful market + fruit stop in the old town when you want a lighter Funchal hour.

days.heading: Fanal fog forest + Porto Moniz lava pools

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Fanal - go only if there IS fog

days.note: This day has a double job: it is the ancient-forest-and-lava-pools loop, and it is the Arieiro backup slot. If Thursday's summit was clouded out, do the sunrise retry first and compress this loop into the afternoon. Fanal without fog is skippable; Porto Moniz is not.

spots.name: Fanal fog forest (Paul da Serra)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · FanalFlickr
spots.cost: Currently free, with a large free lot at the Fanal forestry post. Since Jan 2026 access is designated-paths-only with a daily visitor cap; a paid-entry model is under study - verify closer to travel.
spots.climate: June: Fanal sits at ~1,150 m in the cloud belt - fog is most likely in the morning and on humid days, and June afternoons often burn clear. The fog IS the show; a clear Fanal is just a pasture with old trees.
spots.saveHtml: Save Fanal costs nothing - the save is sequencing. Check the webcams/weather that morning and only commit when fog is actually sitting on the plateau.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Nothing to buy here. Spend the saved money on lunch at the Porto Moniz pools 25 minutes downhill.
spots.restoHtml:
• Restaurante Cachalote — built on the lava rocks beside the pools; burgers and simple grills, the location does the work
  • Restaurante Orca — pool-view terrace; burgers and simple mains
  • Restaurante Santo Antonio — espetada-and-fries dinner stop on the drive back south via Encumeada
spots.altboxHtml:
• Sao Vicente valley drive ↩ — if the plateau is stubbornly clear, drop through the dramatic north-coast valley road instead and get to the pools early.
  • Pico Ruivo from Achada do Teixeira ↗ — shorter back-door summit route if the Arieiro ridge is closed, foggy, or too exposed.
  • Risco waterfall only ↗ — flatter Rabacal branch with a tall waterfall when 25 Fontes feels like too much walking.

spots.name: Porto Moniz natural lava pools
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Porto MonizFlickr
spots.cost: EUR 3 pp for everyone age 3+ = EUR 12 family, open 9 am-7 pm in summer, with changing rooms, lockers, showers, lifeguards, and a snack bar. The rougher Cachalote pools on the west side are free.
spots.climate: June sea: ~70 F - brisk but swimmable, and the lava pools are calm even when the open Atlantic is rough. This is Madeira's one real swim stop; Crete still carries the warm-water week.
spots.saveHtml: Save The paid pools are already the cheap option at EUR 12 for the family - bring towels and swim shoes and skip renting anything.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Lunch on the rocks at Cachalote or Orca with the surf exploding behind the glass - pay for the view once.
spots.restoHtml:

days.heading: Sao Lourenco cliffs, then fly to Lisbon - buffer night
days.daycost: Est. $180-$320 - permits, airport food, Lisbon hotel dinner

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: PR8 to Casa do Sardinha, 8:30 am start

days.note: The trailhead is 10 minutes from the airport, so the east-end cliffs fit cleanly before an afternoon flight. The Lisbon night is the wind-risk shock absorber - if FNC cancels on you, there are ~12 flights the next morning and the Athens chain is still safe. If all goes well, it converts into pasteis and one golden-hour walk.

spots.name: Ponta de Sao Lourenco cliffs (PR8)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Ponta de Sao LourencoFlickr
spots.cost: Permit EUR 4.50 pp (kids 12 and under free) = ~EUR 13.50 family via SIMplifica. Baia d'Abra trailhead parking is free. Casa do Sardinha cafe at km 3 has drinks, snacks, and EUR 1 toilets.
spots.climate: June: the peninsula is exposed, shadeless, and windy - start by 8:30 am, bring hats and water. Family version: hike to the fenced viewpoints (~1 km) or Casa do Sardinha (~3 km) and skip the final Pico do Furado climb.
spots.saveHtml: Save This is the cheapest epic view on the island - EUR 13.50 total. Pack water and snacks instead of relying on the one trail cafe.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge None on the trail. Put the money toward the post-hike pizza terrace in Canical before heading to the airport.
spots.restoHtml:
• Casa do Sardinha (on-trail cafe) — drinks, snacks, and toilets ~3 km into the Sao Lourenco trail - the family turnaround point
  • Pizza Cafe (Machico) — customizable pizzas 10 minutes from the trailhead
  • La Carbonara (Canical) — Italian pizza and pasta with an ocean-view terrace, ideal post-hike
spots.altboxHtml:
• Prainha do Canical black-sand beach ↩ — Madeira's only natural sand beach, 5 minutes from the trailhead - the swap if legs are done but the family still wants the east-end views.
  • Whale Museum Canical ↗ — compact indoor backup five minutes from the east-end coast.
  • Ponta do Rosto viewpoint ↗ — drive-up cliff views if the full Sao Lourenco walk is too windy or hot.

spots.cost: The night exists for flight reliability, not sightseeing: hotel $130-$200, metro/taxi $20-$40, pasteis de nata about EUR 1.50 each. No tickets, no timed entries, nothing bookable to miss.
spots.climate: June Lisbon: around 77-82 F days / 63 F nights and reliably dry - perfect for one unhurried evening walk after four mountain days.
spots.saveHtml: Save Stay airport-area and ride the metro downtown for the evening instead of paying central-Lisbon rates for a bed you use for nine hours.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge One miradouro dinner in Alfama if the FNC flight ran on time - the golden-hour rooftops are the free show, the table is the upgrade.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pasteis de Belem — the original custard tart bakery since 1837 - the whole point of the buffer evening
  • Honorato — Lisbon burger chain; plain burgers, fries, and chicken options
  • ZeroZero — wood-fired pizza chain with several central locations; plain margherita and pasta
spots.altboxHtml:
• Cascais instead ↩ — a 30-40 minute transfer trades the city evening for a beach-town one - fine too, but it adds distance to the Jun 14 morning airport run, so airport-area remains the default.
  • Praia das Macas ↗ — bigger family beach with food nearby if cliff coves feel too exposed.
  • Monserrate Palace ↗ — lush gardens and lighter crowds than Pena; good if timed palace slots are gone.

days.heading: Fly Lisbon to Chania via Athens
days.daycost: Est. $180-$320 - airport food, taxis, first Crete dinner
days.note: Starting this chain from a Lisbon hotel instead of a wind-delayed Madeira gate is the whole reason the buffer night exists. Prefer one protected itinerary; do not land in Athens after midnight and self-connect to Crete on a tight separate ticket.

days.heading: Balos boat from Kissamos

facts.label: Wind swap
facts.valueHtml: Trade days with Elafonissi if needed

days.note: With Chania squeezed to five nights there is no dedicated flex day anymore - Balos and Elafonissi are deliberately back-to-back so they can swap by wind forecast. Keep it public-boat/simple unless the budget is pricing unusually low.

spots.cost: Current 2026 pre-Jul-15 Gramvousa/Balos boat pricing: EUR 40 ages 13+, EUR 24 ages 3-12, plus EUR 1 municipal fee for passengers over 13. Family baseline about EUR 147 before meals.
spots.climate: Mid-June: hot, bright, and exposed. Water should be comfortable enough for real swimming, but shade and wind are the deciding factors.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the public Kissamos boat and bring snacks/water. Driving the rough Balos road adds car-risk and a steep walk back up.

/* NAV */

  .site-nav-menu{height:100%;display:flex;flex-direction:column;min-height:0;overflow:hidden}

  .site-nav-links{flex:1 1 auto;display:grid;align-content:start;gap:6px;overflow-y:auto;overscroll-behavior:contain;-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch;min-height:0;max-height:calc(100vh - 92px);padding:2px 2px 16px;scrollbar-width:thin;scrollbar-color:rgba(246,241,231,.26) transparent}
  .site-nav a{display:flex;align-items:center;min-height:36px;padding:8px 10px;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:8px;background:transparent;font-size:.82rem}

  .site-nav a.nav-home{margin-bottom:6px;background:rgba(42,83,89,.42);color:var(--nav-active);border-color:rgba(95,154,163,.48)}
}
@media(max-width:959px){
  .site-nav{position:sticky;top:0;padding:10px clamp(14px,4vw,22px);background:rgba(23,19,15,.96);border-bottom:1px solid var(--nav-line);backdrop-filter:blur(14px);box-shadow:0 10px 28px rgba(12,10,8,.18)}
  .site-nav-menu{max-width:1180px;margin:0 auto}
  .site-nav summary{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:14px;min-height:42px;padding:8px 12px;border:1px solid var(--nav-line);border-radius:10px;background:var(--nav-panel);box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(12,10,8,.22);color:var(--nav-text);font-size:.84rem;font-weight:900;cursor:pointer}
  .site-nav summary::after{content:"+";display:grid;place-items:center;width:24px;height:24px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--nav-active);color:var(--nav-active-ink);font-size:1rem;line-height:1}
  .site-nav-menu[open] summary{border-color:rgba(95,154,163,.55)}
  .site-nav-menu[open] summary::after{content:"-"}
  .site-nav-links{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(145px,1fr));gap:7px;margin-top:8px;max-height:min(70vh,480px);overflow:auto;padding:8px;border:1px solid var(--nav-line);border-radius:12px;background:linear-gradient(180deg,var(--nav-panel),var(--nav-bg));box-shadow:0 18px 42px rgba(12,10,8,.34)}
  .site-nav a{display:flex;align-items:center;min-height:42px;padding:9px 10px;border:1px solid var(--nav-line);border-radius:8px;background:rgba(246,241,231,.06);font-size:.82rem}
  .site-nav a.nav-home,.site-nav a:hover{background:var(--nav-active);color:var(--nav-active-ink);border-color:var(--nav-active)}
}
main{max-width:1180px;margin:0 auto;padding:56px clamp(18px,5vw,60px) 40px}
.section-label{text-align:center;margin:0 auto 40px;max-width:760px}
.section-label h2{margin:.2em 0 .3em;font-size:clamp(1.9rem,4.4vw,3rem);font-weight:600}
.section-label p{margin:0;color:var(--muted)}
.divider{margin:78px 0 40px}
/* OVERVIEW */
.overview{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(230px,1fr));gap:18px;margin-bottom:26px}
.ocard{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:16px;padding:22px;box-shadow:var(--shadow)}
.ocard .eyebrow{color:var(--c1)}
.ocard h4{margin:0 0 6px;font-size:1.4rem;font-weight:600}
.ocard p{margin:0;color:var(--muted);font-size:.92rem}
/* TRIP MAP */
.hc-grid{display:grid;gap:12px}
.hc{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(150px,220px) minmax(0,1fr);column-gap:22px;row-gap:6px;width:100%;background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-left:5px solid var(--muted);border-radius:12px;padding:16px 18px;box-shadow:0 10px 28px rgba(30,32,28,.08)}
.hc.actnow{border-left-color:#c0392b}
.hc.watch{border-left-color:var(--gold)}
.hc.good{border-left-color:var(--c3)}
.hc-tag{grid-row:1/3;align-self:start;justify-self:stretch;display:block;font-size:.66rem;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:4px 10px;border-radius:999px;margin:0;color:#fff;text-align:center}
.hc.actnow .hc-tag{background:#c0392b}
.hc.watch .hc-tag{background:var(--gold)}
.hc.good .hc-tag{background:var(--c3)}
.hc h4{grid-column:2;margin:0;font-size:1.15rem;font-weight:600;line-height:1.15}
.hc p{grid-column:2;margin:0;font-size:.9rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.5}

/* TRAVEL TIPS */
.tips-order{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:16px;padding:18px 20px;box-shadow:var(--shadow);margin-bottom:22px}
.tips-order p.mini-h{margin:0 0 12px}
.tips-order ol{margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;counter-reset:step}
.tips-order li{counter-increment:step;position:relative;background:var(--paper);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:999px;padding:7px 14px 7px 30px;font-size:.82rem;font-weight:600}
.tips-order li::before{content:counter(step);position:absolute;left:6px;top:50%;transform:translateY(-50%);width:18px;height:18px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--c1);color:#fff;font-size:.68rem;font-weight:800;display:grid;place-items:center}
.tips-order li span{color:var(--muted);font-weight:600}
.tips-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(340px,1fr));gap:18px}
.tipcard{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:16px;padding:20px 22px;box-shadow:var(--shadow);border-top:4px solid var(--c1)}
.tipcard.t2{border-top-color:var(--c2)}.tipcard.t3{border-top-color:var(--gold)}.tipcard.t4{border-top-color:var(--c3)}
.tipcard h4{margin:0 0 4px;font-size:1.2rem;font-weight:600}
.tipcard .sub{margin:0 0 12px;font-size:.74rem;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.04em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--muted)}
.tipcard ul{margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none;display:grid;gap:11px}
.tipcard li{font-size:.88rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.5;padding-left:16px;position:relative}
.tipcard li::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;top:8px;width:6px;height:6px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--gold)}
.tipcard li b{color:var(--ink)}
.tipcard li.flag::before{background:#c0392b;width:8px;height:8px;top:7px}
.tipcard li.flag b{color:#b5361f}

.daycost{display:inline-block;margin:8px 0 0;font-size:.76rem;font-weight:700;color:var(--c2);background:rgba(194,90,58,.1);border:1px solid rgba(194,90,58,.28);border-radius:999px;padding:3px 11px}
.budget-tbl.grand tr.total td{background:var(--ink);color:#fff;font-size:1.05rem;font-weight:800}
.rate-note{margin:12px 2px 0;font-size:.78rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.5}

.kv.climate{margin-top:10px;padding-top:10px;border-top:1px dashed var(--line)}
.kv.climate span{color:var(--c1)}

/* TIMING COMPARE */
.timing-compare{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(280px,1fr));gap:18px;margin-bottom:22px}
.tcard{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:16px;padding:20px 22px;box-shadow:var(--shadow);border-top:4px solid var(--muted)}
.tcard.now{border-top-color:var(--c1)}
.tcard.later{border-top-color:var(--c2)}
.tcard.best{border-top-color:var(--c3)}
.tcard.best .tlabel{background:var(--c3)}
.tcard .tlabel{display:inline-block;font-size:.7rem;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:3px 10px;border-radius:999px;margin-bottom:10px;color:#fff}
.tcard.now .tlabel{background:var(--c1)}
.tcard.later .tlabel{background:var(--c2)}
.tcard h4{margin:0 0 12px;font-size:1.25rem;font-weight:600}
.tcard .trow{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:14px;padding:7px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);font-size:.88rem}
.tcard .trow:last-child{border-bottom:0}
.tcard .trow span{color:var(--muted)}
.tcard .trow strong{text-align:right}
.tcard .trow strong.bad{color:#b5361f}
.listcard.pro-list{border-top:4px solid var(--c3)}
.listcard.con-list{border-top:4px solid #c0392b}
.listcard.pro-list li::before{content:"✓";position:static;width:auto;height:auto;border-radius:0;background:none;color:var(--c3);font-weight:800;margin-right:6px}
.listcard.con-list li::before{content:"✗";position:static;width:auto;height:auto;border-radius:0;background:none;color:#c0392b;font-weight:800;margin-right:6px}
.listcard.pro-list li,.listcard.con-list li{padding-left:0;display:flex;gap:2px}
.listcard.pro-list li>span,.listcard.con-list li>span{flex:1}
.verdict-box{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-left:5px solid var(--ink);border-radius:14px;padding:20px 22px;box-shadow:var(--shadow);margin-top:20px}
.verdict-box h4{margin:0 0 8px;font-size:1.1rem;font-weight:800}
.verdict-box p{margin:0 0 10px;font-size:.92rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.55}
.verdict-box p:last-child{margin-bottom:0}
.verdict-box .aside{font-size:.82rem;font-style:italic;border-top:1px dashed var(--line);padding-top:10px;margin-top:12px}

.tripmap-wrap{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:20px;padding:14px;box-shadow:var(--shadow)}
.mapbtns{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px}
.mapbtns button{border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);font-weight:700;font-size:.82rem;padding:7px 14px;border-radius:999px;cursor:pointer;transition:.15s}
.mapbtns button:hover{background:var(--ink);color:#fff}
.mapbtns button .sw{display:inline-block;width:9px;height:9px;border-radius:50%;margin-right:6px;vertical-align:middle}
#tripmap{height:460px;border-radius:14px;z-index:1}
.leaflet-popup-content{font:14px/1.4 "Inter",sans-serif}
.leaflet-popup-content b{font-family:"Fraunces",serif}
.pin{width:16px;height:16px;border-radius:50%;border:2.5px solid #fff;box-shadow:0 1px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.5)}
/* BASES */
.bases{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(260px,1fr));gap:20px}
.base{position:relative;background:var(--card);border-radius:18px;overflow:hidden;box-shadow:var(--shadow);border:1px solid var(--line)}

.base.b1 .band{background:var(--c1)}.base.b2 .band{background:var(--c2)}.base.b3 .band{background:var(--c3)}

.base .bbody{padding:18px 20px 22px}
.base .nights{display:inline-block;padding:3px 10px;border-radius:999px;font-size:.72rem;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:.06em;color:#fff;margin-bottom:10px}
.base.b1 .nights{background:var(--c1)}.base.b2 .nights{background:var(--c2)}.base.b3 .nights{background:var(--c3)}
.base h4{margin:0 0 4px;font-size:1.55rem;font-weight:600}
.base .dates{margin:0 0 10px;color:var(--muted);font-size:.85rem;font-weight:600}
.base p{margin:0;color:var(--muted);font-size:.9rem}
.base .book{margin:12px 0 0;padding-top:12px;border-top:1px solid var(--line);font-size:.82rem;color:var(--ink)}
.base .book b{color:var(--c2)}
/* PLAN GRID */
.plan-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:20px}
.pcard{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:16px;padding:22px 24px;box-shadow:var(--shadow)}
.pcard h4{margin:0 0 14px;font-size:1.3rem;font-weight:600;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px}
.pcard h4 .dot{width:10px;height:10px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--gold)}
.prow{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:16px;padding:8px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);font-size:.9rem}
.prow:last-of-type{border-bottom:0}
.prow span{color:var(--muted)}.prow strong{text-align:right}
.pcard .tip{margin:12px 0 0;padding:10px 12px;background:rgba(217,164,65,.12);border-radius:10px;font-size:.82rem;color:#8a6a1e}
/* DAYS */
.days{display:grid;gap:26px}
.day{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:20px;overflow:hidden;box-shadow:var(--shadow);border-left:6px solid var(--c1)}
.day.c1{border-left-color:var(--c1)}.day.c2{border-left-color:var(--c2)}.day.c3{border-left-color:var(--c3)}.day.c0{border-left-color:var(--muted)}

.day-title h3{margin:2px 0 4px;font-size:1.4rem;font-weight:600;line-height:1.05}

.logistics{padding:4px 24px 12px}
.facts{display:grid;margin:6px 0 12px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden}
.facts div{display:grid;grid-template-columns:64px 1fr;gap:12px;padding:9px 13px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);font-size:.86rem}

.facts span{color:var(--muted);font-size:.68rem;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;padding-top:2px}
.facts strong{font-weight:600}
.note{margin:0;color:var(--ink);font-size:.94rem;line-height:1.55}
/* SPOTS */
.spots-wrap{display:grid;gap:20px;padding:6px 24px 24px}
.travel-note{padding:40px;text-align:center;color:var(--muted);border:1px dashed var(--line);border-radius:14px;font-weight:600}
.spot{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:16px;overflow:hidden;background:var(--paper)}
.spot-head{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:10px;padding:14px 16px}
.spot-name{margin:0;font-size:1.22rem;font-weight:600}
.explore{display:flex;gap:6px;flex:0 1 auto;min-width:0;max-width:100%;overflow-x:auto;overscroll-behavior-x:contain;-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch;scrollbar-width:none}

.explore .xi{background:linear-gradient(45deg,#f09433,#dc2743 55%,#bc1888)}
.explore .xf{background:#0063dc}

.carousel{position:relative;overflow:hidden;background:#e7e1d4}
.track{display:flex;overflow-x:auto;scroll-snap-type:x mandatory;scroll-behavior:smooth;scrollbar-width:none}
.track::-webkit-scrollbar{display:none}
.track figure{margin:0;flex:0 0 100%;scroll-snap-align:center;position:relative}
.track img{display:block;width:100%;aspect-ratio:3/2;object-fit:cover;background:#e7e1d4}
.track figcaption{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;padding:26px 14px 10px;color:#fff;font-size:.74rem;line-height:1.3;background:linear-gradient(180deg,transparent,rgba(0,0,0,.68))}
.track figcaption strong{display:block;font-weight:700}
.track figcaption span{color:rgba(255,255,255,.82);font-size:.66rem}
.nav{position:absolute;top:50%;transform:translateY(-50%);width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:50%;border:0;background:rgba(255,255,255,.86);color:var(--ink);font-size:1.4rem;line-height:1;cursor:pointer;display:grid;place-items:center;box-shadow:0 4px 14px rgba(0,0,0,.25);transition:.15s;z-index:2}
.nav:hover{background:#fff;transform:translateY(-50%) scale(1.08)}
.nav.prev{left:12px}.nav.next{right:12px}
.counter{position:absolute;top:12px;right:12px;background:rgba(0,0,0,.55);color:#fff;font-size:.72rem;font-weight:700;padding:4px 10px;border-radius:999px;z-index:2}
.dots{position:absolute;bottom:10px;left:0;right:0;display:flex;justify-content:center;gap:6px;z-index:2;flex-wrap:wrap;padding:0 40px}
.dots .dot{width:7px;height:7px;border-radius:50%;border:0;background:rgba(255,255,255,.5);cursor:pointer;padding:0;transition:.15s}
.dots .dot.on{background:#fff;width:20px;border-radius:999px}
/* SPOT GRID */
.spot-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1.15fr) minmax(0,.85fr);gap:18px;padding:16px}
.mini-h{margin:0 0 6px;font-weight:800;font-size:.76rem;letter-spacing:.04em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--muted)}
.kv{margin-bottom:12px}
.kv span{font-weight:800;font-size:.78rem;color:var(--ink)}
.kv p{margin:4px 0 0;font-size:.9rem;color:var(--muted)}
.callout{border-radius:10px;padding:10px 12px;font-size:.86rem;margin-bottom:10px;line-height:1.45}
.callout b{font-weight:800}
.callout.save{background:rgba(63,125,78,.1);border-left:3px solid var(--save)}
.callout.save b{color:var(--save)}
.callout.splurge{background:rgba(217,164,65,.14);border-left:3px solid var(--splurge)}
.callout.splurge b{color:var(--splurge)}
.resto{margin:14px 0 4px}
.resto ul{margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none;display:grid;gap:8px}
.resto li{font-size:.85rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.4;padding-left:14px;position:relative}
.resto li::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;top:7px;width:6px;height:6px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--gold)}
.resto li a{text-decoration:none}.resto li b{color:var(--ink)}
.altbox{margin:14px 0 4px;padding:12px;background:rgba(31,111,120,.07);border-radius:10px}
.altbox p:last-child{margin:0;font-size:.86rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.45}
.altbox a{text-decoration:none}
.bloglinks{margin-top:14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px}
.bloglinks a{font-size:.83rem;text-decoration:none;color:var(--c1);font-weight:600}
.bloglinks a:hover{text-decoration:underline}
.spot-map{display:flex;flex-direction:column}
.mapwrap{position:relative;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--line);flex:1;min-height:240px}
.gmap{width:100%;height:100%;min-height:240px;border:0;display:block}
.gmap-btn{margin-top:10px;text-align:center;background:var(--ink);color:#fff;text-decoration:none;font-weight:700;font-size:.85rem;padding:10px;border-radius:10px;transition:.15s}

      <h2>Madeira does the epic hiking, Crete does the warm swimming</h2>

    <div class="hc-grid">
      <div class="hc good"><span class="hc-tag">Verdict</span><h4>Madeira is the right scenery-and-hiking swap</h4><p>The family wants epic scenery and real hikes from the Portugal leg, not Atlantic swimming. Madeira delivers the <b>Pico do Arieiro stairway ridge above the clouds</b>, 25 Fontes, Fanal's fog forest, and Sao Lourenco's cliffs - things the mainland simply does not have - while Crete still supplies all the <b>73-74 F</b> swim days.</p></div><div class="hc watch"><span class="hc-tag">Branch cost</span><h4>What this costs vs. the mainland version - honestly</h4><p>Compared to the Portugal + Crete plan: <b>+1 PTO day (8 vs 7)</b>, roughly <b>+$700-$1,500 in flights</b> (extra FNC legs and losing simple round-trip pricing; estimated, not quoted) plus <b>~$150-$250</b> for the buffer night, Chania squeezed <b>6 -> 5 nights</b> (the weather flex day is gone), Rethymno <b>3 -> 2</b>, and new FNC wind exposure. That's the full price of the stairway - decide with eyes open.</p></div><div class="hc actnow"><span class="hc-tag">Wind rule</span><h4>Never chain FNC to Athens in one day</h4><p>Funchal is the only airport in the world with a mandatory certified wind limit, and studies show wind-restriction episodes peak <b>in summer</b> - June 9, 2026 alone saw 22 cancellations. Prefer an <b>early-afternoon FNC-LIS departure</b>: evening flights are the ones stranded when afternoon winds build.</p></div><div class="hc watch"><span class="hc-tag">Cloud lottery</span><h4>Arieiro is a weather gamble - 4 nights buys 2 shots</h4><p>The sea-of-clouds sunrise happens when a morning inversion sits below the 1,818 m summit; clouds usually swallow the peaks by afternoon. Save money

  • Enforce the flight gate. Quote the whole chain (PIT-FNC, FNC-LIS, LIS-ATH-CHQ, return) before booking anything; above $6.9k family, fall back to the mainland version - that alone saves $850-$1,750.
  • Kids hike nearly free. Madeira trail permits are free for 12-and-under, so the 8-year-old pays EUR 0 across PR1, PR6, and PR8; the family total for all three epic trails is about EUR 59.
  • Self-drive the sunrise. Driving to Arieiro at 5:15 am instead of buying four transfer seats saves roughly $120-$160 and keeps the cloud-lottery schedule flexible.
  • Cable car one-way, toboggan down. Riding up (EUR 48) and tobogganing/taxiing down beats the EUR 76 round trip and is more fun anyway.
  • Boat Balos, do not private-charter it. The public Kissamos boat keeps the signature Crete day near EUR 147 before meals.
  • Use apartments everywhere. Breakfasts, laundry, and simple dinners are how 12 hotel nights stay inside a $3.1k lodging ceiling.
  • Choose CHQ or HER by return fare. Rethymno is central enough to support either airport if the savings are real.

Worth the splurge

  • The Monte toboggan (EUR 80). Two wicker sleds down a Funchal street - the most kid-memorable EUR 80 on Madeira.
  • Guided Arieiro sunrise transfer (EUR 30-40 pp). Worth it if nobody wants to drive dark mountain hairpins at 5 am.
  • Espetada dinner in Estreito. Skewers, fries, and bolo do caco at Santo Antonio - a splurge that is also picky-kid-proof.
  • Well-located Chania lodging. Paying a bit more for beach/parking access reduces daily friction across five nights.
  • One polished final dinner in Rethymno. Save the restaurant splurge for the last warm evening, not every night.

Travel Tips

The stuff nobody tells you

Operational notes from July 2026 research; reconfirm tickets, permits, and schedules when 2027 inventory opens (~11 months out, late summer 2026).

Book in roughly this order

  1. All flight legs and baggage · first - this is the go/no-go gate for the whole branch
  2. Madeira automatic rental car · with the flights; June automatics sell out 3-6 months ahead
  3. Funchal and Chania lodging · after flights; refundable, apartment-first
  4. SIMplifica trail permits (PR1, PR6, PR8) · as soon as 2027 dates open; morning slots sell out days ahead
  5. Lisbon buffer hotel · refundable - it is the wind shock absorber
  6. Crete rental car · early, automatic and insurance confirmed
  7. Balos boat + Rethymno lodging · after Crete dates and return airport are fixed
  8. Kourtaliotiko/Preveli and Fanal access rules · recheck 30-60 days out; both are in regulatory flux

Flight Chain & Wind

The part that can make or break the branch

  • One protected outbound ticket. PIT to FNC must be a single PNR - TAP via Lisbon or United via Newark if the seasonal EWR-FNC nonstop returns for 2027.
  • Never chain FNC to Athens same-day. Funchal wind restrictions peak in summer; the Lisbon buffer night is structural. Fly FNC-LIS early/mid-afternoon, not on the last evening flight.
  • Quote as one system. Price every leg together before assuming the budget works; above $6.9k family, fall back to the mainland version.

Madeira Permits & Timing

The fussy bookables, 2026 rules

  • SIMplifica or turned away. All classified PR trails need pre-booked permits with a 30-minute entry window: PR1 EUR 10.50, PR6/PR8 EUR 4.50, kids 12 and under free.
  • Arieiro is a morning game. The cloud sea is an inversion phenomenon - summit by sunrise, and keep Saturday as the swap slot if Thursday is socked in.
  • Toboggans close Sundays. Carreiros do Monte runs Mon-Sat, cash only, EUR 40 per 2-person sled - which is why it anchors Wednesday's arrival evening.

Driving Two Islands

Freedom, not stress

  • Madeira roads are serious. 20% grades, hairpins, 100+ tunnels: low gear downhill, film the walkaround, take full coverage - mountain-road damage is the #1 rental dispute.
  • Do not drive the Balos road. The public boat avoids the rough track, the parking scramble, and the uphill hike back with tired kids.
  • Parking beats views. In both Funchal and Chania, an apartment with known parking beats a charming one with nightly car anxiety.

Food Fit

Picky-eater coverage is strong on both islands

  • Every stop has a safe order. Pizza, pasta, burgers, fries, and grilled chicken are confirmed at Funchal, Camara de Lobos, Porto Moniz, Machico, Lisbon, Chania, and Rethymno.
  • Madeira's local dish is kid food. Espetada is beef-on-a-skewer with fries and soft bolo do caco bread; prego rolls and milk-and-honey chicken are equally safe.
  • Greek grills stay the fallback. Chicken souvlaki, pita, fries, and plain rice cover every Crete night; apartment breakfasts cut both cost and morning friction.

Money Gate

When to trim instead of stretching

  • Flights over $6.9k kill the branch. That is not a trim trigger - it is the signal to book the mainland Portugal + Crete version instead and bank the difference.
  • Lodging over $3.2k is a warning. Move from pool/view premium to apartment-first before touching trip length.
  • First trims: private extras. Skip the Balos private options, Monte Palace garden, and paid beach sets before cutting a base or a day.

Weather Reality

Two lotteries, one plan

  • Arieiro: 4 nights = 2 shots. Thursday is the attempt, Saturday is the retry. If both mornings fail, that is the accepted risk - the levadas and coast do not care about clouds.
  • Fanal is best IN fog. Check conditions that morning; a clear Fanal is skippable, and the pools are the guaranteed half of that day.
  • Crete wind swaps, not cancels. Balos and Elafonissi sit back-to-back on Wed/Thu so the boat day can chase the calmer forecast.

What People Are Saying

Insider notes from people who've actually gone

Crowd-sourced from Reddit, TripAdvisor, AllTrails, and local-run blogs (July 2026) — the off-the-beaten-path stuff guidebooks skip. Reconfirm permits, tides, and prices closer to travel.

Madeira above the clouds

The ridge, timed right

  • The Stairway photo is better in the afternoon. Everyone crowds Arieiro for a cold, hazy sunrise; the local secret is 1–2 hrs before sunset for soft light and thin crowds.
  • Real headlamps, not phone lights. The PR1 ridge and the 25 Fontes / Rabaçal route run through long pitch-black tunnels; every family member needs a dedicated light.
  • Kid-sized levada. If the ridge is too much, PR11 Levada dos Balcões (Ribeiro Frio) is short, flat, wide, and ends at a mountain lookout — easy with kids.

Madeira: pools & poncha

Coast-side reality checks

  • Check the Porto Moniz webcam before driving out. Swell slams the lava pools without warning; the sea is calmest in the morning and best at higher tide. Water shoes are essential on the razor rock — the free "Piscinas do Aquário" nearby is where locals swim.
  • Drink poncha where locals do. Skip the sweet passion-fruit tourist versions; ask for the traditional fisherman's poncha (rum, lemon, honey) at old-school spots like Taberna da Poncha or the hillside A Venda do André — and go slow, it's stronger than it tastes.
  • Toboggan up by 9am, cash in hand. Waits at Monte hit two hours after 10am and the wicker-sled drivers often take cash only.

Crete beaches: beat the buses

Turquoise ones fill by 10

  • Balos & Elafonissi before 9:30am or after 4pm. Cruise ships and tour buses land midday (noon–5); go early or late for calm water, soft light, and open parking. June shoulder season is your edge — far quieter than July–August.
  • Elafonissi's lagoon is a toddler's dream — knee-deep and warm for hours. Use only the official €5 lots; roadside "helpers" waving you into private lots get aggressive.
  • Falasarna is a morning beach. Calmest, most vivid turquoise before the wind picks up after ~2pm. If Elafonissi's packed, cedar-lined Kedrodasos next door is the escape valve.

Chania & Rethymno like a local

One street back

  • Leave the Venetian harbor for dinner. Family tavernas in the inner alleys — Splantzia and Koum Kapi in Chania, Petychaki Square in Rethymno — serve real Cretan food at a fraction of the harbor price.
  • Cretan meals are meant to be shared. Ask for half portions; nearly every dinner ends with a free raki and dessert on the house.
  • Carriers, not strollers, in the old towns. Cobbled pedestrian alleys make a stroller near-useless.

blocks.title: Reserve cars and transfers
items: Reserve a Madeira rental car for FNC pickup/drop with an automatic if needed, strong brakes, full insurance, and hotel parking confirmed.
Reserve the Crete rental car for CHQ pickup and CHQ/HER return once the return airport is final.
Decide whether to hire a transfer/guide for PR1 sunrise if mountain-road driving before dawn feels like the wrong kind of adventure.
Reserve PIT parking or a ride plan for the Tue Jun 8 evening departure.

blocks.title: Trail permits, boats, and hard-to-move activities
items: Jan 15: create/check the Madeira SIMplifica account and confirm the 2027 PR trail reservation rules.
Mar 15: reserve the Balos Lagoon boat for Wed Jun 16, with Elafonissi/Falasarna as the wind swap.
May 10: book PR1 Arieiro/Ruivo access for Thu Jun 10 as soon as the relevant window allows; morning slots go first.
May 11-13: book PR6/25 Fontes and PR8 Sao Lourenco permits or guided alternatives for the planned Madeira dates.
May 15: make one Rethymno last-dinner reservation for Sun Jun 20.

blocks.title: Documents, insurance, money, and phones
items: Check all passports by Jan 15. Target validity through at least Dec 21, 2027 for a clean buffer.
Check ETIAS status by Feb 1 and apply through the official EU site once it is live for 2027.
Buy travel insurance by Jan 31 and make sure it covers flight delays, missed connections, and Madeira weather disruption.
Get International Driving Permits by Apr 15 for all possible drivers.
Set up eSIM/international roaming, credit-card travel notices, and no-foreign-fee payment cards.

blocks.title: Final two-week run-up
items: May 18: reconfirm flight times, FNC car pickup, trail status, hotel parking, and Crete car pickup hours.
May 25: download offline maps for Madeira, Lisbon airport area, Chania, and Rethymno.
Jun 1: check Madeira webcams/weather patterns and keep the Arieiro retry logic alive.
Jun 7: pack passports, IDPs, trail shoes, layers, headlamps, swimsuits in carry-ons, motion-sickness meds, adapters, and printed trail/boat confirmations.

preDepartureTodos.callout: Do not forget: this route depends on the Lisbon buffer night. It is the protection against FNC wind delays and should not be sacrificed for a prettier spreadsheet.
